The real scandal? Both parties let SNAP become a bloated bureaucratic nightmare while ignoring systemic waste. Cutting $30 billion from nutrition programs might grab headlines, but it’s a drop in the ocean compared to the $1.7 trillion in annual discretionary spending funneled through broken agencies.

The Farm Bill’s $33 billion deficit spike proves Washington’s addiction to reckless spending isn’t partisan—it’s institutional. Instead of performative cuts or handouts, how about auditing the USDA’s $154 billion budget where millions vanish into redundant admin costs and overpriced contracts?

Reform starts with shredding the red tape, not rearranging deck chairs on this sinking fiscal Titanic.
